note: Hand-derived from reducer.ExtractSymbolRuntimeIntentRows's real extraction path over symbol_runtime_family_odu.go's fixture, filtered to the runs_in domain's upsert rows, fanned out against reducer.ExtractWorkloadCandidates -> reducer.BuildProjectionRows's WorkloadRows for the same repository. This fixture proves LIVE that the family is not merely a one-edge assertion that cannot distinguish 'processed every route-bound function' from 'processed only the first one': HandleWidgets (GET+POST /widgets, deduped to one row by runs_in's own functionID+repoID dedupe key, which has no method dimension) and HandleHealth (GET /healthz, a distinct handler on a distinct path) both bind, yielding TWO edges. A regression that stopped after the first resolved handler would silently drop the HandleHealth edge, and this exact-set assertion would catch it as MISSING by name. The repository DEFINES exactly one Workload here, so the fan-out this fixture exercises per-row is still 1-row-to-1-edge (2 rows, 2 edges, not a cross product). The live Cypher's (Repository)-[:DEFINES]->(Workload) MATCH carries no LIMIT, so the WRITE TEMPLATE would permit an N-Workload fan-out -- but today's reducer.ExtractWorkloadCandidates/BuildProjectionRows cap a single repository at exactly one Workload (workload signals aggregate per repo_id, and one WorkloadRow is emitted per candidate), so no live fixture can currently exhibit two Workloads for one repository to prove that direction end to end. The general N-Workload cross product this guard would still compute correctly if the projection ever contained one is proven deterministically by a synthetic offline unit test instead (materialized_edges_runs_in_test.go), not by adding a second Workload to this live fixture, per the coordinator's explicit instruction that the honest single-workload case is sufficient here. source_entity_id is each handler's canonical Function uid (content.CanonicalEntityID) -- the same function_id HANDLES_ROUTE resolves for the same handler, since runs_in reuses the identical handlesRouteEntries route data. target_entity_id is the deterministic (non-hashed) workload id BuildProjectionRows derives: "workload:" + the repository's Name field (WorkloadName is never set in this fixture, so it falls back to RepoName) -- the SAME workload id for both edges, since both handlers belong to the one repository/one Workload. SCOPE LIMIT: reducer.ExtractWorkloadCandidates -> reducer.BuildProjectionRows, which this fixture's guard runs to derive the Workload id above, is a pure projection seam only -- it is NOT the live correlation/admission engine the workload-materialization handler actually routes every candidate through (CorrelatedWorkloadProjectionInputLoader.LoadWorkloadProjectionInputs -> admittedCorrelatedWorkloadCandidates -> deployableUnitRulePack's rule-pack selection). This Odù carries a Dockerfile file fact PLUS a Jenkinsfile file fact specifically so its candidate selects JenkinsRulePack (admits on structural evidence alone) rather than DockerfileRulePack (which a bare Dockerfile signal would select, and which rejects this candidate outright at MinAdmissionConfidence 0.90 plus a required dockerfile/image evidence pair this Odù never emits) -- a live determinism run with only the Dockerfile fact committed zero Workload nodes even though this offline guard reported success. The live determinism gate remains the sole authority for whether the admission engine actually committed the Workload node these edges MATCH against; this fixture only proves the projection and extraction seams reproduce correctly.
